classification.difficultyReason: Choose to calculate the rhombus area from the rectangle-sized diagonals, derive a side from midpoint lengths using Pythagoras, then reinterpret that side as a base and reverse A=bh to obtain the oblique height.

inlines.text: A rhombus sits inside a rectangle with side lengths 11 cm and 7 cm. The vertices of the rhombus are at the midpoints of the sides of the rectangle.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 6 figure, below the prompt on the left
spec.description: Unshaded horizontal rectangle with a rhombus joining its side midpoints. All four rhombus sides have matching single ticks. The segment h joins the bottom midpoint to the upper-right rhombus side; its right-angle marker at the bottom midpoint is against the parallel lower-left side.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle dimensions are 11 cm by 7 cm. Rhombus diagonals are 11 cm and 7 cm. The height endpoint is the orthogonal projection of the bottom midpoint onto the upper-right rhombus side.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied dimensions, equality marks, right-angle mark and unknown h are visible.

answer.worked:
The rhombus diagonals are the rectangle’s side lengths.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{xy}{2}\\A&=\frac{11\times7}{2}\\A&=38.5\,\text{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
The midpoints give a right triangle with legs $5.5$ cm and $3.5$ cm. Let the rhombus side length be $b$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=\sqrt{5.5^2+3.5^2}\\b&=\sqrt{42.5}\,\text{cm}\end{align*}$$
Using the side as the base,
$$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\38.5&=\sqrt{42.5}\,h\\h&=\frac{38.5}{\sqrt{42.5}}\,\text{cm}\\h&\approx5.91\,\text{cm}\quad\text{(2 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$
